segments.arabic: [571] حدثنا معاذ بن فضالة قال: حدثنا هشام عن يحيى عن أبي سلمة عن جابر بن عبد الله
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Fadalah related to us. He said: Hisham related to us, from Yahya, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah:

segments.arabic: أن عمر بن الخطاب جاء يوم الخندق بعد ما غربت الشمس فجعل يسب كفار قريش قال: يا رسول الله ما كدت أصلي العصر حتى كادت الشمس تغرب قال النبي ﷺ والله ما صليتها فقمنا إلى بطحان فتوضأ للصلاة وتوضأنا لها فصلى العصر بعد ما غربت الشمس ثم صلى بعدها المغرب
segments.english: That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came on the day of the Ditch after the sun had set and began cursing the unbelievers of Quraysh. He said: “Messenger of Allah, I barely managed to pray ‘Asr before the sun was about to set.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Allah, I have not prayed it.” We got up and went to Buthan. He performed ablution for the prayer, and we performed ablution for it. He prayed ‘Asr after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.

notes: The selected barely/about-to-set wording is retained, distinct from the shorter until it set in 573. Both ablutions, the oath, place and prayer order remain. The Khan-family rendering of Umar’s statement is not used to erase that distinction.

segments.arabic: وأقم الصلاة لذكري

segments.english: And Habban said: Hammam related to us. Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the like of it.

segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Awf related to us. He said: Abu al-Minhal related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: انطلقت مع أبي إلى أبي برزة الأسلمي، فقال له أبي حدثنا كيف كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي المكتوبة قال: كان يصلي الهجير وهي التي تدعونها الأولى حين تدحض الشمس ويصلي العصر ثم يرجع أحدنا إلى أهله في أقصى المدينة والشمس حية
segments.english: I went with my father to Abu Barzah al-Aslami. My father said to him: “Tell us how the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the prescribed prayer.” He said: “He used to pray the midday prayer—which you call the first—when the sun declined, and he prayed ‘Asr, then one of us would return to his family in the furthest part of Madinah while the sun was bright.”

segments.arabic: ونسيت ما قال في المغرب
segments.english: And I have forgotten what he said about Maghrib.

segments.arabic: قال: وكان يستحب أن يؤخر العشاء قال: وكان يكره النوم قبلها والحديث بعدها وكان ينفتل من صلاة الغداة حين يعرف أحدنا جليسه ويقرأ من الستين إلى المائة
segments.english: He said: “He liked to delay ‘Isha’.” He said: “He disliked sleeping before it and conversation after it. He used to finish the morning prayer when one of us could recognise the person sitting beside him, and he would recite from sixty to a hundred.”

segments.arabic: [575] حدثنا عبد الله بن الصباح قال: حدثنا أبو علي الحنفي حدثنا قرة بن خالد قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Sabbah related to us. He said: Abu ‘Ali al-Hanafi related to us. Qurrah ibn Khalid related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: انتظرنا الحسن وراث علينا حتى قربنا من وقت قيامه فجاء، فقال دعانا جيراننا هؤلاء،
segments.english: We waited for al-Hasan, and he was late in coming to us until we were close to his time for rising. He came and said: “These neighbours of ours invited us.”

segments.arabic: ثم قال: قال أنس
segments.english: Then he said: Anas said:

segments.arabic: نظرنا النبي ﷺ ذات ليلة حتى كان شطر الليل يبلغه فجاء فصلى لنا ثم خطبنا، فقال ألا إن الناس قد صلوا ثم رقدوا وإنكم لم تزالوا في صلاة ما انتظرتم الصلاة
segments.english: We waited for the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night until it was approaching half the night. He came and led us in prayer, then addressed us, saying: “Indeed, the people have prayed and then gone to sleep, while you have continued in prayer as long as you have waited for the prayer.”

segments.arabic: قال الحسن وإن القوم لا يزالون بخير ما انتظروا الخير
segments.english: Al-Hasan said: “People continue to be in good as long as they wait for good.”

segments.arabic: قال قرة هو من حديث أنس عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Qurrah said: “It is from Anas’s hadith from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.”

notes: The opening wait, al-Hasan’s delay and neighbours’ invitation, Anas’s account and both closing attributions remain. Ibn Hajar explains the rising time as the usual end of al-Hasan’s gathering and yablughuhu as approaching; neither a start-of-teaching gloss nor a new narrator chain for that verb is introduced.
The closing Qurrah attribution is kept as an explicit transmission remark rather than silently merging al-Hasan’s preceding sentence into the Prophetic quotation.

segments.arabic: [576] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: حدثني سالم بن عبد الله بن عمر وأبو بكر ابن أبي حثمة أن عبد الله بن عمر قال
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar and Abu Bakr ibn Abi Hathmah related to me that ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ صلاة العشاء في آخر حياته فلما سلم قام النبي ﷺ، فقال أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه فإن رأس مائة لا يبقى ممن هو اليوم على ظهر الأرض أحد فوهل الناس في مقالة رسول الله ﷺ إلى ما يتحدثون من هذه الأحاديث عن مائة سنة وإنما قال النبي ﷺ لا يبقى ممن هو اليوم على ظهر الأرض يريد بذلك أنها تخرم ذلك القرن
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed ‘Isha’ near the end of his life. When he had given the greeting of peace, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: “Consider this night of yours: at the end of a hundred, no one who is on the face of the earth today will remain.” The people misunderstood the statement of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, taking it to mean what they say in these accounts about a hundred years. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, only said: “No one who is on the face of the earth today will remain,” intending by that the passing away of that generation.

notes: The selected Abu Bakr ibn Abi Hathmah is retained without supplying Sulayman from the comparison. The first hundred has no explicit unit in the selected paragraph or modern print, unlike the historical print; years is therefore not inserted there. The second occurrence explicitly says a hundred years.
The misunderstanding and generation explanation remain within Ibn Umar’s account, outside the Prophetic quotation. No additional end-of-world or lifespan explanation is inserted.

segments.arabic: [577] حدثنا أبو النعمان قال: حدثنا معتمر بن سليمان قال: حدثنا أبي حدثنا أبو عثمان عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي بكر
segments.english: Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. He said: Mu‘tamir ibn Sulayman related to us. He said: My father related to us. Abu ‘Uthman related to us, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr:

segments.arabic: أن أصحاب الصفة كانوا أناسا فقراء وأن النبي ﷺ قال: من كان عنده طعام اثنين فليذهب بثالث وإن أربع فخامس أو سادس وأن أبا بكر جاء بثلاثة فانطلق النبي ﷺ بعشرة قال: فهو أنا وأبي وأمي
segments.english: That the people of the Suffah were poor people, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever has food for two should take a third, and if for four, then a fifth or a sixth.” Abu Bakr brought three, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went off with ten. He said: “It was I, my father and my mother,”

segments.arabic: فلا أدري قال وامرأتي وخادم بيننا وبين بيت أبي بكر
segments.english: I do not know whether he said: “And my wife and a servant shared between us and Abu Bakr’s household.”

segments.arabic: وإن أبا بكر تعشى عند النبي ﷺ ثم لبث حيث صليت العشاء ثم رجع فلبث حتى تعشى النبي ﷺ فجاء بعد ما مضى من الليل ما شاء الله قالت له امرأته وما حبسك عن أضيافك أو قالت ضيفك قال أو ما عشيتيهم قالت أبوا حتى تجيء قد عرضوا فأبوا قال: فذهبت أنا فاختبأت، فقال: يا غنثر فجدع وسب، وقال كلوا لا هنيا، فقال والله لا أطعمه أبدا وأيم الله ما كنا نأخذ من لقمة إلا ربا من أسفلها أكثر منها
segments.english: Abu Bakr ate supper with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then remained where ‘Isha’ was prayed. Then he returned and stayed until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ate supper. He came after as much of the night had passed as Allah wished. His wife said to him: “What kept you from your guests?”—or she said: “Your guest.” He said: “Did you not give them supper?” She said: “They refused until you came. It was offered to them, but they refused.” He said: “I went and hid.” He said: “Ghunthar!” Then he invoked mutilation against me and insulted me, and said: “Eat, without enjoyment!” He said: “By Allah, I will never eat it.” By Allah, whenever we took a morsel, more than it grew from beneath it.

segments.arabic: قال يعني حتى شبعوا وصارت أكثر مما كانت قبل ذلك
segments.english: He said, meaning: until they were full and it had become more than it was before.

segments.arabic: فنظر إليها أبو بكر فإذا هي كما هي أو أكثر منها، فقال لامرأته يا أخت بني فراس ما هذا قالت لا وقرة عيني لهي الآن أكثر منها قبل ذلك بثلاث مرات فأكل منها أبو بكر، وقال إنما كان ذلك من الشيطان
segments.english: Abu Bakr looked at it, and it was as it had been, or more. He said to his wife: “Sister of Banu Firas, what is this?” She said: “No, by the joy of my eye, it is now three times more than it was before.” Abu Bakr ate some of it and said: “That was only from Satan,”

segments.arabic: يعني يمينه
segments.english: meaning his oath.

segments.arabic: ثم أكل منها لقمة ثم حملها إلى النبي ﷺ فأصبحت عنده وكان بيننا وبين قوم عقد فمضى الأجل ففرقنا اثنى عشر رجلا مع كل رجل منهم أناس الله أعلم كم مع كل رجل فأكلوا منها أجمعون
segments.english: Then he ate a morsel of it and carried it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and it remained with him until morning. There was an agreement between us and some people, and its term expired. He divided us among twelve men, with people accompanying each of them—Allah knows how many were with each man—and they all ate from it,

segments.arabic: أو كما قال
segments.english: or as he said.

notes: The food counts, wife/servant uncertainty, guest/guests alternative, oaths, repeated eating and waiting, narrator explanations, treaty, twelve men and final uncertainty all remain. The uncertainty includes the wife and servant here, following both English comparisons and the related commentary; modern punctuation can restrict it to the wife. Its scope remains provisional.

Both inspected prints and the selected digital text read haythu, where, in the Isha clause. The English comparisons use until, a documented alternative Arabic reading; that alternative is not silently substituted. The repeated supper/return sequence stays in its selected order without importing the nap variant.

Ghunthar is retained as a harsh address rather than selecting one disputed English insult. Ibn Hajar explains jadda as a curse invoking mutilation, not a physical act; the following insult and uncomfortable eat without enjoyment wording are retained. The joy-of-my-eye phrase is kept as an oath rather than an address to Abu Bakr. Divided us among twelve men follows the commentary’s grouping reading, without adding military leaders or naming an unstated subject.
